name: Pak-Tong
world_status: statement found in an open source

earlier_scan.source_named: Blust, Robert 2021, 'Pak', in Eight languages of the Admiralty Islands, Papua New Guinea (hhtype=wordlist;specific_feature) - not found online; all other refs are wordlists

new_statements.quote: As the foregoing phonetic transcriptions show, stress was recorded as final in some forms and penultimate in others, However, there was no indication that it is phonemic. In most words it was recorded as final. This was true of all the numerals that contain at least two syllables, and of several directly possessed body-part terms, such as [purúk] ‘my head’. However, after the first 15-20 forms were recorded, I stopped writing stresss consistently, and where I later recorded it sporadically it was sometimes penultimate, as with [múwon] ‘male; man’, and [píhɪn] ‘female; woman’.
new_statements.citation: Blust, Robert. 2021. Sketch 7: Pak. In Eight Languages of the Admiralty Islands, Papua New Guinea, 481-546. Language & Linguistics in Melanesia Special Issue 2021 (ISSN 0023-1959). Port Moresby: Linguistic Society of Papua New Guinea.
new_statements.locator: sec. 7.2 Phonology, printed p. 485 (PDF p. 6), final paragraph of the section; txt lines 248-255
new_statements.rule_in_words: Word stress is non-contrastive and predominantly on the final syllable (all polysyllabic numerals, singular-possessed body-part nouns), with some tokens recorded penultimate; the author flags that stress was only transcribed systematically for the first 15-20 forms, so the generalisation is tentative.
new_statements.secondary_stress: One four-syllable form, dienpeliew [díjɛnpɛliɛ̀w] 'thigh', was recorded with initial primary stress and a secondary stress on the final syllable (same page); the 1975 field packet p.208 also marks putúnminèk, lolhónminèk (penult-of-stem primary, final secondary). No rule stated.
new_statements.exceptions: Penultimate stress in [múwon] 'man', [píhɪn] 'woman'; initial primary in [díjɛnpɛliɛ̀w] 'thigh'. Author states there is no indication stress is phonemic and that his later stress marking was sporadic.
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated elicited words (citation forms) from a modified Swadesh list plus possessive paradigms; 8.25 contact hours with three teenage speakers of the Mulireu (Pak island) dialect, March 1975 (sketch misprints 1971; intro p.15 gives 1975). No phrase-level discussion.
new_statements.identity_note: Blust 2021 describes the Pak-island dialect (Mulireu village) of Pak-Tong (pakt1239, ISO pkg); the Tong-island dialect was not recorded. The earlier world scan named this same source as unreachable; it is open access as a per-sketch PDF on the Language & Linguistics in Melanesia site (LLM Special Issue 2021), not an Academia Sinica or print-only volume.

Consistent with the 2021 sketch.
